beats: The last truck leaves. Every level at par and every sighting found.
The Perfect Game card pops up. Hard-hat confetti behind it.
Three big hard hats pop in, one by one.
The Zero Incident medal on the shoulder.
Every sighting found: 40 of 40.
The Company Man appears...
...and, for the first time ever, smiles. “Huh. Not bad.”
One button: Crew photo.
Tap.
The crew is lined up on the strip, facing a camera on a tripod. Slow Moe peers through it.
“Squeeze in!”
He sets the self-timer. Beep... beep...
Hurries to his spot.
Hop-turn. Big grin, thumbs up.
The magpie flies in...
...and lands on his hard hat.
Moe’s eyes roll up. Frozen grin. Don’t move.
Beep-beep-beep-beep.
Tail up.
SPLAT. FLASH. At the same moment.
The photo drops onto the screen: the crew, smiling; Moe, eyes up, splat on his hat.
Heh heh. The magpie is very pleased.
It flies off.
Moe glares after it. “Seriously?”
The screen goes dark. The photo slides up to the top.
The credits roll up under it.
“Thanks for playing.” Holds.
Fade back up: the empty lease. The crew has gone; the biffy’s light is red.
rows: The bison, the bull and the cow
in the making of this game.

beats: The empty lease. Quiet. Only the biffy to look at, its light red.
The view closes in on the biffy.
Creeeak. The door swings open.
Slow Moe leans out: bathrobe, pyjamas, slippers, hard hat, brushing his teeth.
Stops. Notices you.
Takes the toothbrush out. “You’re still here?”
“Shift’s over. Go home.”
Brush back in. Scrub scrub. Leans back in.
Creeeak. The door shuts.
Fade to the game’s own opening screen, exactly as when the app opens: the cover image with the roughneck and his wrench, RIG JAM, TAP TO START.
